title: Polygamy and Concubines
lead: Many men in the Old Testament had more than one wife or kept concubines (secondary wives, often slaves). The Bible records the practice without directly forbidding it in the law, but its stories show the rivalry and grief it brought, and Jesus and Paul point back to one man and one woman (Genesis 2:24; Matthew 19:4–6; 1 Timothy 3:2).

sections.b: The first polygamist is Lamech, a violent man (Genesis 4:19–24). Abraham's, Jacob's and Elkanah's households are torn by rivalry between wives (Genesis 16; 29–30; 1 Samuel 1:6). The law regulates the practice: a man may not marry two sisters as rivals (Leviticus 18:18), must give the less-loved wife's firstborn his rights (Deuteronomy 21:15–17), and the king must not multiply wives (Deuteronomy 17:17). Solomon's many wives turn his heart away (1 Kings 11:1–4). Jesus answers questions about marriage from Genesis 2:24 (Matthew 19:4–6), and church leaders are to be "the husband of one wife" (1 Timothy 3:2).
